state_limits: Child HEAD equals parent pin; git status --short --untracked-files=all was empty. No notebooks, training, private corpus or GPU execution was accessed.
description: A research archive exploring explicit learned key-value memory read/write modules for toy binding and pointer tasks and byte-level prediction.
scope_audience: Personal exploratory research on whether a small memory bank can preserve and retrieve bindings; README states it is incomplete, unpublished and not maintained.

creativity.reason: The memory-bank experiment is an interesting adaptation, but the project itself identifies a known architecture family and does not establish novelty.

current_usefulness.reason: A self-contained toy notebook is documented, but it is impractically slow and no reproducible converged result or baseline is supplied.

expected_usefulness.reason: If completed on exactly computable tasks with baselines, the experiment could answer a bounded memory-learning question; intended positive outcomes are not assumed.

impl_progress.reason: Memory cells and data/training paths are implemented, but notebooks lack saved execution outputs, held-out metrics and several required corpora.

presentability.reason: README provides a reading order, architecture description and candid replay limits; there is no packaged or reproducible research result.

verification: README and representative kb.py implementation inspected; notebooks, embedded images, training curves and corpora were not read or run.

evidence.locator: The architecture, concretely; What is here vs. not

contribution: Source defines read/write memory and toy-task paths, showing an actual research attempt; it does not establish convergence, task benefit or novelty.
alternatives_question: Which established external-memory or recurrent-memory approaches solve the same exact binding and pointer-chain tasks, and what controlled result would distinguish this implementation?

delivery_likelihood.reason: The archive is frozen, main training data is unavailable and the documented self-contained run is prohibitively slow without changes.

reason: The implemented experiment supports retaining a research attempt, while useful outcome and novelty remain unknown and the recorded limitations are substantial.
next_step: If revived, choose one synthetic task, add a tractable implementation and baseline, and save revision-bound held-out results.
inspection_limits: No source projects were changed, installed, built, executed, tested, or accessed over a network; no child commits or pushes were made.

All initialized child repositories matched their parent gitlink and had empty `git status --short --untracked-files=all`; this does not inspect ignored/generated data. The local_lm_research submodule was reported uninitialized and left unknown.
The parent repository revision advanced during this investigation; `parent_revision` records the observed revision at report completion. Assigned child gitlink pins remained unchanged.

No public alternatives research or global novelty claim is included. All implementation/runtime, visual, security and performance claims are limited to inspected source or explicitly attributed project documentation; the parent owns external comparisons and synthesis.
For learn_draw, only structural product intent and source were inspected; private/personal payloads, target imagery, artwork and live work records were excluded.
